headline: Computational methods infer cell states and niches from single-cell and spatial omics
label: Single Cell Computational Methods
summary: Recent preprints extend single-cell and spatial inference to histology, multi-omics and epigenetic age, with explicit uncertainty and resolution control.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of cell identity, state and tissue context from single-cell, spatial and histological data, with several items addressing how confidently those inferences can be made. BiNVaST performs cell typing across Xenium, CosMx and Stereo-seq platforms using a niche boundary-preserving variational autoencoder, while GOLDEN decomposes spatial spots into target and nontarget fractions to address genetic heterogeneity. Optimal transport soft couplings score per-cell match uncertainty in single-cell multi-omics. scOmnom adds automated clustering-resolution selection with auditable outputs. Learned representations bridge modalities in VGL-stGen and ALHENA, which distill transcriptomic foundation model knowledge into an H&E encoder, though a virtual spatial transcriptomics benchmark finds predicted uncertainty largely redundant with the predicted mean. Other items apply related logic to clinical and biological questions, including HRDPath and EG-BINN.
